subject: R 4.0.2 Update and Proj6 - altered mesh and predictions

messages.author: eafa26121223327e
messages.subject: R 4.0.2 Update and Proj6 - altered mesh and predictions
parts:
Hi,

I've recently upgraded my program R from 4.0 to 4.0.2. I've also begun rerunning some SPDE models for publication edits that were submitted in late 2019. Many of the spatial projection commands in the code now result in warnings, specifically: 

In proj4string(loc) : CRS object has comment, which is lost in output
2: In proj4string(loc.domain) :
  CRS object has comment, which is lost in output

I understand from a previous post mid-summer that most of these warnings are probably a non-issue. However, I've also noticed that despite running the same exact code over the same files, (e.g. changing nothing), the size of my mesh has changed slightly, and model output has changed as well. Even more of an issue are the drastic changes I see in the predictions that we generate from the final models. While they are identical to previous files in some areas, they are about half the value in others. The process I'm using to generate the predictions is developed from Fuglstad's (2017) suggested code, so I would expect some level of variation since we had to rerun the simulations. But, I would definitely not expect to see the level of variation that is being produced currently. 

To further verify that there is in fact a difference between the versions and not the code, we've also rerun the models within an R 4.0 environment again. We get identical model output to that which we'd published in our manuscript, and predictions are much more on target with what we would expect from the model parameters. 

If anyone has any suggestions as to what could be causing the difference and how to resolve the issue, I would really appreciate the input. The only thing I can think of was that INLA is acting differently somehow within the 4.0.2 environment and that it has something to do with the introduction of PROJ6. Even if that's the case though, I unfortunately don't know enough about the program to address the issue.

Thanks in advance,
KK

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R 4.0.2 Update and Proj6 - altered mesh and predictions
parts:
Hi,
I wouldn’t expect the R version itself to make a difference. Far more important is the versions of the INLA, rgdal, and sp packages, since the major code changes are due to the proj6 transition in rgdal and sp.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R 4.0.2 Update and Proj6 - altered mesh and predictions
parts: Code written for proj4 can in some cases completely fail to do the right thing with proj6, since not all old proj4string information survives in the translation. The warning you see may fall in that category, but if need to actually run the code in debug mode to know for sure.

Finn

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R 4.0.2 Update and Proj6 - altered mesh and predictions
parts:
To follow up on Finn’s comments, we also slightly tighten the step-size for numerical gradient/Hessian calculations from control.inla=list(h=0.01) to h=0.005, which in cases where the posterior is flat, might cause minor differences, but to the better. In these ‘flat’ cases I would suggests to rerun if you’re unsure, with

r=inla(…)
r= inla.rerun(r)

Other than the proj6 and related issues, there no changes which are due to the transition R-3.6 to R-4.0 which should cause your problem.  I guess you’re running the latest testing version, if not, please do.

H

-- 
Håvard Rue
